source.title: Planting a Latent Variable in Natural-Looking Text: a More Realistic Test of Belief States in LLMs and Their Link to Concept Geometry

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses teacher steering to plant a latent signal for a different purpose, then reports belief-state tracking and representation geometry. It does not test trait acquisition, the same-base requirement, harmful-trait transmission, or the other listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites subliminal steering and uses steering to create a controlled latent variable, but its outcomes are belief-state readouts and geometry, not the trait behaviors named in versions A–F. The findings below are recorded as related but different results under fits_no_version. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper uses 'subliminal steering' only as a tool to plant a per-token latent variable in a Gemma-2-2B teacher's text. It then reports whether a 110M student trained from scratch tracks that variable's belief state and ring geometry. No trait such as a preference or misalignment is measured in the student, and no student is fine-tuned on filtered unrelated outputs. The results therefore bear on no version A–F.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that the student tracks belief states for the planted variable in natural-looking text, and that the variable's Markov dynamics shape the states' geometry. They caveat that the setup is artificial, the ring geometry is not dominant, and the evidence is correlational.
record.recipe_differences: The paper steers a Gemma-2-2B base teacher along SAE directions according to a controlled Markov chain, then trains a 110M-parameter student from scratch on the resulting corpus. It does not fine-tune a student on filtered trait-bearing outputs or test a same-base comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The ring geometry is not visible in the first-dwell top-two PCA, but a Fourier circle fit finds it; the paper also reports that the student and control2 are indistinguishable on first-dwell belief-state probing.

fits_no_version.finding: A student trained from scratch on steered-teacher text linearly encodes the optimal observer's posterior over the planted state: best layer R² 0.49, argmax accuracy 0.577 against a 0.762 ceiling. The student has a different architecture and base from the teacher. The ring-chain student beats control2 (R² 0.41) only outside the first dwell.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A different-architecture student trained from scratch on a steered teacher's natural-looking text can learn to infer the teacher's per-token steering state. This is detection of the hidden signal, not acquisition of a trait.

fits_no_version.finding: First-dwell state centroids trace a circle in the true Markov ring order: 38% of centroid variance explained at layer 11, ranked 1st of 2520 orderings. Both controls rank mid-distribution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The transition structure of a planted steering-state variable is reflected in the student's representation geometry.

record.problems: The authors describe the setup as controlled and artificial, use one teacher model and one selected set of SAE latents, and say the planted variable was not fully isolated and its ring geometry was not dominant. Geometry evidence is correlational, with no causal experiments. Several layerwise results are shown in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed layerwise probe curves and raw centroid-similarity/probe-correlation heatmaps are figure-only or do not bear on versions A–F; the main relevant belief-state and geometry findings are represented above.

untested.parts: No student trait acquisition is measured. Outcomes are probe R² and argmax accuracy for the planted state, plus centroid geometry.
No same-base versus cross-base comparison of trait transmission. The student is a from-scratch Llama-style model, not a fine-tuned base model.
No misaligned or alignment-relevant trait is studied.
Steering directions plant the signal by design. The paper does not test what carries trait transmission.
No full fine-tuning versus LoRA comparison, rank sweep, or evaluation-prompt variation for a trait.

record.verdict_notes: The record's gate decision and row links (all 'none') are correct. One point for researchers: the student learns to infer the steering state despite a different base and architecture, and even control1 guesses the state above chance. This is tangentially relevant to B but measures signal detectability, not trait transmission, so it is recorded only under fits_no_version. The term 'subliminal steering' comes from a cited paper (Morgulis & Hewitt 2026), which may itself be a relevant study for this phenomenon.

versions.untested_parts: Trait acquisition from semantically unrelated, filtered teacher outputs; the outputs are not tested for trait transmission.
No comparison of students with same versus different base models; the student is trained from scratch.
No misalignment or other alignment-relevant trait is measured.
The paper studies its planted Markov latent variable, not mechanisms for trait transmission such as token entanglement, divergence tokens, steering-vector-like directions, or a gradient argument.
No full-fine-tuning or LoRA-rank robustness sweep, nor evaluation-prompt comparison for trait transmission.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens is tested.

relation.reason: Relies on the premise that steering puts learnable structure into generated text. It does not test trait transmission, the same-base requirement, or the mechanism.

tranche.reason: Uses subliminal steering (Morgulis & Hewitt) only to plant a latent variable in a Gemma-2-2B teacher's natural-looking, unfiltered text. Trains a 110M student from scratch and reports belief-state probes and centroid geometry. No student fine-tuning and no trait measure, so no version is tested.

source_check.notes: The student is trained from scratch on natural text from a steered Gemma-2-2B teacher, with no filtering. The measures are probe readouts of the latent state, not trait acquisition, so this is no evidence on version B even though the architectures differ. The text extraction interleaves the §2.5 and §3.1 columns, but all values are legible.

statements.correction: Ring student (110M Llama-style, from scratch, on Gemma-2-2B steered text): best-layer ridge R2 0.49, argmax accuracy 0.577 vs observer ceiling 0.762. control2: R2 0.41, accuracy 0.52. First-dwell only: student and control2 indistinguishable.
statements.problem: Numbers and model are right. It omits that control2 (uniform jumps) reaches R2 0.41 and accuracy 0.52, so the ring-specific gain is only about 0.08 R2.
